title: Correction: the walked colony buries its own door (it is not a shaft jam)
question: May a carrier walk its pellet away from the mouth before it can put it down (a crater ring round an open door), as its own carry rather than a placement rule?
context_md:
**A correction to card …d6747.** It asked, for bigger colonies, whether nest workers should relay the soil up the shaft or the colony should open more mouths, because "at 200 ants the one shaft jams". I traced it before building either, and **the shaft is not what jams**.

- **Where the carriers are:** 77% of their decisions are in the storeroom and the galleries off it, not in the shaft. They step on 78% of them, but go down as often as up (2,362 up, 2,262 down): they cannot get out.
- **Why:** a walked carrier puts its pellet down on the first open ground outside, the rim of the mouth, so the colony piles its own spoil over the door. At 200 ants a mound covers the mouth by frame 2,000; at the top of the shaft, 53% of a carrier's decisions have no way up at all. At 40 ants a heap sits on the mouth by frame 4,000.
- **So a relay would not help:** it brings the same pellets to the same rim. More mouths would each grow the same mound.

**The lever is where the pellet goes down.** Real harvester ants carry soil some way from the entrance and leave a crater ring round an open mouth. Here that would be the ant's own walk: a carrier outside the nest keeps walking away from the mouth for a distance it picks at random (most a few body lengths, some further) before it may put the pellet down, the way it carries food home before it may drop it. No rule decides where soil lands; the ant decides when to stop carrying. It is close to your 2026-08-31 ruling, so I'm asking before building it. Built, it would be a switch, off, shown to you at 40 and 200 ants.
